title: A Real Warning About Delaying Marriage
author: Institute for Family Studies
source: Institute for Family Studies Digest, March 27, 2026
summary: IFS research reveals that the timing of marriage matters significantly for long-term relationship stability and satisfaction. Young adults who delay marriage into their late 20s and 30s often face different social and relational conditions than those who marry earlier. The research shows that those who marry very young face higher divorce rates, but those who delay too long may miss the window for family formation or find fewer suitable partners. The widespread cultural message that young adults should delay marriage indefinitely may obscure the genuine goods of earlier commitment and the practical advantages of starting family formation while partners are younger and more flexible.
points: The timing of marriage significantly affects relationship stability and long-term satisfaction.
Delaying marriage too long can result in missing the family formation window.
Young adults who marry in their mid-to-late 20s report higher satisfaction than those who delay indefinitely.
Cultural messaging about indefinite delay may obscure the real costs of perpetual postponement.
quotes: A real warning about delaying marriage: timing matters more than the culture acknowledges.
Those who delay marriage too long often face a narrowed pool of partners and shifted expectations.
The research suggests an optimal window for marriage—not too young, but not too late.” Archived from Institute for Family Studies Digest on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
